channel.description: Nature is the foremost international weekly scientific journal in the world and is the flagship journal for Nature Portfolio. It publishes the finest peer-reviewed research in all fields of science and technology on the basis of its originality, importance, interdisciplinary interest, timeliness, accessibility, elegance and surprising conclusions. Nature publishes landmark papers, award winning news, leading comment and expert opinion on important, topical scientific news and events that enable readers to share the latest discoveries in science and evolve the discussion amongst the global scientific community.

item.title: [8] Anomalous metal and superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Joshua Folk, Matthew Yankowitz

Authors: Anna Okounkova, Abigail Sohm, Tobias Faehndrich, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experiment on correlated superconductivity in moire systems.

Tags: #superconductivity #graphene #correlated-electrons

Abstract: Observations of rhombohedral graphene on a WSe2 substrate at varying temperature, magnetic field and current indicate the presence of regions of gate space with zero-resistance superconductivity alongside others with finite saturation resistance.

item.title: [6] Stacking-induced direct band gap in CVD-grown 1H MoS2 bilayers
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Kuang-I Lin, Yann-Wen Lan

Authors: Tilo H. Yang, I-Tong Chen, Min-Jia Zhang, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study on 2D TMD materials and band structure engineering.

Tags: #2D-materials #TMD #electronic-structure

Abstract: Atomically aligned 1H bilayer MoS2 exhibits a direct band gap, enhanced excitonic emission and stronger valley polarization, establishing its potential for advanced optoelectronic and valleytronic applications.

item.title: [6] Organic two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Thomas Heine, Xinliang Feng

Authors: Anupam Prasoon, Nguyen Ngan Nguyen, Mike Hambsch, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Methodological development in van der Waals heterostructure assembly.

Tags: #vanderWaals #heterostructure #2D-materials

Abstract: Sequential on-water-surface assembly enables layer-by-layer stacking of two-dimensional polymers to create both lattice-matched and controlled lattice-mismatched van der Waals heterostructures with defined lattice registry, stacking sequence and thickness.
